# Test fixtures

**No disk image is committed to this repository, in any form.** That is
[D-010](../../Docs/DECISIONS.md), Accepted 2026-08-22, and it has no exceptions
and no whitelist. `.gitignore` excludes disk-image extensions repository-wide;
committing one requires a decision entry, not a negation line.

This directory holds a manifest and documentation. Nothing else.

## Where the fixtures are

Built in code, by [`ade-fixtures`](../../tools/fixtures), at test time:

```rust
use ade_fixtures::{Volume, corrupt};

let mut v = Volume::dd(0).named("Workbench");   // DOS\0, OFS
let f = v.add_file("startup-sequence", b"echo hello");
let root = v.root();
let mut img = v.build();

corrupt::hash_chain_loop(&mut img, f);          // AV-001
```

Three reasons this beats storing binaries, in short: a generator says what it
builds where a blob says nothing; it emits dostypes no real collection contains
(the 4288-image survey has no `DOS\4`, `DOS\6` or `DOS\7`); and structures like
hash-chain loops and out-of-range pointers do not occur on genuine disks at
all, so they were always going to be constructed. The full reasoning, including
what this approach does *not* cover, is in D-010.

## The differential corpus

Real images live outside version control — by convention in `disks/` at the
repository root, which is gitignored. Tests that need them **skip cleanly when
they are absent**, so a fresh clone builds and passes with no corpus and no
network.

```
cargo test                      # generated fixtures only
cargo test -- --nocapture       # also reports what the corpus tests skipped
```

The consequence worth stating plainly: **CI never exercises a real Amiga disk.**
It verifies that the specification is implemented, not that reality matches the
specification — and those differ, as
[SPEC §Corpus observations](../../Docs/SPEC.md) records. Running the corpus
locally is therefore a habit, not an optional extra.

## corpus.manifest

Not present until differential tests reference specific images. When it is, the
format is one row per image:

```
sha256                                                            size    name
```

Generated by:

```bash
cargo run -p ade-fixtures --bin manifest -- disks/ > tests/fixtures/corpus.manifest
```

Names and hashes are metadata, not content, so committing them distributes
nothing copyrighted. The point is reproducibility: "this image fails" is only
actionable if the image can be identified exactly by someone holding their own
TOSEC set.
